data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'theos' (God) and 'opisthen' (behind), signifying one who has divine insight or god-given vision. The name Theopista carries the meaning “Divine Sight, God-given Vision” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Theopista usually hope their child will grow to embody divine sight, god-given vision and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Θεόπιста
in_greek.long_meaning: Θεόπιστα είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από τη φωνή Θπιστγ, που σημαίνει 'Θεός/Θεία Καλός/Ἀρχή/Ἀγγέλος'. Το όνομα μπορεί να περιλαμβάνει την έννοια της αγιοσύνης, της αρχηγικής, της ομορφιάς και της αυτοσυνειδησίας. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο άγγελος Μάζορ, ο οποίος ήταν Χριστιανός, ο οποίος ήταν Χριστιανός, ο οποίος ήταν Χριστιανός, ο οποίος ήταν Χριστιανός - όλοι αυτοί είναι οι ίδιοι. Από την άλλη πλευρά, υπάρχουν ορισμένα από τα στοιχεία της Κιβουθρωσιάς, όπως, 'οι όροι που ονομάζουν με Θεόπιστα, δηλαδή, 'ο Άγιος, ο αρχηγός, ο ομορφός, και ο αυτοσυνειδητός'.

historical_references.reference: Theopista of Thessalonica was a prominent Christian woman who lived in the late 4th to early 5th century. She was known for her piety and charitable works, and was considered a model of Christian virtue. According to legend, she was martyred during the reign of Emperor Arcadius (395-408 AD), when she was seized and tortured for refusing to renounce her faith.

Another Theopista, also known as Theopista of Cyzicus, was a powerful Christian woman who lived in the 6th century. She was a relative of Emperor Anastasius I (491-518 AD) and held significant political influence. She is said to have used her power to protect Christians during the reign of Emperor Zeno (474-491 AD), who was known for persecuting non-Chalcedonian Christians.
